links.outcome: Proportion of PCPs who received any AI training versus those prioritizing AI training
links.effect: 88.2% (150/170) identified AI training as a priority, but only 26.5% (45/170) had any training; training experiences varied widely in source, focus, and structure.
links.quote: Though 88.2% (150/170) identified AI training as a priority, only 26.5% (45/170) had any training.

links.outcome: Clinician confidence in understanding AI bias sources and ethical issues
links.effect: Confidence in understanding sources of AI bias was 36.5% (62/170) and ethical issues 47.6% (81/170); few gave accurate technical AI definitions.
links.quote: Confidence in understanding sources of AI bias (62/170, 36.5%) and ethical issues (81/170, 47.6%) was limited.

screen.reason: National cross-sectional survey evaluating clinicians' knowledge, attitudes, use, and training needs regarding AI in health care.
